assistant_message_replied_to.text:
Phase 1 is done: the evaluation harness is built, tested, and run on the real inputs as a dry run only. Nothing was fitted, scored or evaluated on any real event, and no holdout outcome was read. The work is in two commits in the NRE repo, `a1f6c2c` (code and tests) and `200a4ea` (logs, report, docs). CI passed on Python 3.12 and 3.13 for both. Locally the full suite is 742 tests, exit status 0, 4 skipped as before.

**What the dry run showed** (`reports/m4-harness-dry-run-2026-10-06.json`):
- All 18 integrity checks on the protocol and its pinned inputs pass.
- Fold counts and development statuses agree exactly with the freeze record, with no disagreement.
- The two consequences the protocol stated in advance reproduce: `loses_half_of_gap` is `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` in the clean-window version, and `gap_ge_5pct` has exactly 10 pooled positives.
- Every fold has 12.01 to 19.0 days of label-maturity slack, so no purge is needed.
- The holdout shows 23 events sealed, 0 refused reads and 0 loads. The experiment and holdout-access logs hold only their genesis records.

**How the tests were checked:**
- The eight tests the protocol requires are in `tests/test_m4_harness.py`.
- I broke the harness on purpose in 45 ways, and every one makes a test fail. Four were missed on the first run, so I added tests for them. `scripts/m4_mutation_check.py` reproduces this.

**Corrections to myself:**
- A few of my own test expectations were wrong (an average-precision value, a misquoted protocol phrase). The code was right each time.
- A Python patch script again put a real newline into a test line, for the second time. I caught it by running the module straight away, and it is now saved in memory.

**Two things you should know about the holdout:**
- The ordinary loader would have opened all 23 block-5 label files just to check their hashes. I built a separate loader that never opens them. A test destroys all 23 files and the dry run is byte-identical, so the line in the authorization record that the dry run reads no block-5 outcome is literally true.
- The seal is a process control, not secrecy. Anyone can open the files. What it guarantees is that no harness code path reads them except the logged look. Two switches, `ALLOW_REAL_EVALUATION` and `ALLOW_HOLDOUT_LOOK`, are both `False`, and a test fails if either is turned on without that test being changed too.

**Where the protocol was silent:** the code had to settle 12 details, listed in section 5 of `docs/M4-HARNESS.md`. None depends on an outcome. Five could move a result:
- the "wider of the two" headline interval is read as greater width;
- the regression issuer-history mean has no default when no earlier event exists, so the code stops, and the ridge model cannot be finished until you decide;
- whether standardization uses the population or sample standard deviation;
- a predictor that fails in one fold takes that state for its whole pooled result;
- the group prior follows the same maturity and earlier-session rules as the issuer's own history.

**What remains:**
- **You:** decide on those five (accept the defaults, or amend the protocol as a new version before Phase 2). The earlier review items still stand: the two thin primary targets, the 99% claim level, and a counts-only holdout.
- **Me, not authorized yet:**
  - Phase 2: the other baselines (C2, C3, C4, the logistic and ridge models and their without-sector variants).
  - Phase 3: the C0-clock baselines.
  - Phase 4: the single holdout look, the descriptive report that includes block-5 counts, and the Milestone 4 report. Accepting Milestone 4 is your decision.

My recommended next step is that you read section 5 of `docs/M4-HARNESS.md` (about ten minutes), start with the regression-mean default, and then decide whether to authorize Phase 2. Recommending it does not authorize it.

Details are in `docs/M4-HARNESS.md` and `reports/m4-phase1-completion-2026-10-06.json`.

new_in_phase_2.detail: Standardization uses the population standard deviation (divide by n). A feature whose standard deviation is zero, to within floating-point rounding (1e-12), is dropped and the drop is logged.

The regression issuer-history mean has no default when no earlier event exists (the protocol gives only the binary rate p = 0.5). M3 is fitted on the training events with the target defined AND an issuer-history mean; the few earliest training events with no earlier matured event are left out of the fit, counted and logged for each fold, and nothing is substituted for them. They still count as history for later events. Every test event has a history mean (checked by the structure audit before the run); if one did not, the run would stop.
The history features of a training row are computed point-in-time inside the training set (earlier, matured training events only), exactly as for a test event.

Newton-Raphson starts at the zero vector. Linear systems are solved by Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting, and a pivot below 1e-12 in absolute value is MODEL_FIT_FAILED. Convergence (largest absolute coefficient change below 1e-8) and the 100-iteration limit are the protocol's; failure is MODEL_FIT_FAILED and nothing is substituted.

Predictions and fitted parameters are rounded to 12 decimal places when produced, so that results reproduce across platforms (the C libraries behind exp and log can differ in the last bit). Metrics are computed from the rounded predictions.

The monotone repair caps each M2 variant's gap_ge_5pct probability at that same variant's gap_ge_3pct probability for the same event (M2_logistic by its own, M2_without_sector by its own). A missing 3% prediction makes the 5% model MODEL_FIT_FAILED. Every repair is counted and logged for each fold.

Contrasts reported: every predictor against C1; M2 against C2, C3, C4 and M2_without_sector; M3 against C2, C3 and M3_without_sector; and M2 or M3 against C1 in each development fold. The one confirmatory contrast per primary target is the clean-window M2_logistic (binary) or M3_ridge_linear (regression) against C1; the all-event contrast of the same pair is its companion in the status rule. Every other contrast is labelled exploratory.
Each use of the C2 or C3 fallback to the pooled value (a cell with fewer than 10 defined training events) is counted for each fold and for each test event, and logged.

The without-sector sensitivities remove only the two sector indicators, as the protocol defines them. The issuer-history feature's group prior still uses the SIC major group where at least 10 earlier events share it, so a sector dependence remains in M2_without_sector and M3_without_sector.
Only the three B-clock primaries can be evaluated on the real inputs: the tripwire is restricted to those targets, and a C0 target is refused until Phase 3 is authorized.

not_a_claim: Not a result: nothing beyond the pooled base rate on synthetic data has been evaluated when this record is written.
Not a statement that any predictor will beat the base rate: the protocol expects most primaries to be NOT_DISTINGUISHABLE.
